column1: # 🔴 REFUSAL 1 — AND IT IS THE FIGURE p377's OWN "28 %" RESTED ON.

column2: p377 published HolonIQ at $12.3 B as "the high end of 2026".  A targeted leg at HolonIQ returns NO AI-in-education figure at all.  HolonIQ's own pages size the BROAD market: EdTech to $404 B by 2025, total education near $10 T by 2030.  Grade: ZERO outlets carry the $12.3 B attribution, including the publisher it names.  🔴 REFUSED, not softened — and with it goes the top end of p377's 28 % spread, which was therefore a spread between a sourced figure and an unsourced one.

column1: # 🔴 REFUSAL 2 — A CATEGORY ERROR, not a disagreement.

column2: Technavio publishes an INCREMENT, not a market size: "forecast to increase BY USD 4.03 billion at a CAGR of 59.2 % between 2024 and 2029" (and USD 2 321.8 mn for 2023-2028).  The $3.37 B circulating for 2025-2030 is of the same shape and was NOT found at the outlet.  🔴 An increment compared against a level is a category error, and any shelf that ranks it beside $9.58 B is comparing a delta with a total.

column1: # 🔴 REFUSAL 3 — a doubled figure attributed to a publisher this base quotes DIRECTLY.

column2: A third-party statistics page attributes "$23 B in 2026, fastest-growing segment at +42 % CAGR" to Grand View Research.  This base carries Grand View at $11.4 B for 2026, derived from GVR's own $57.2 B/2033 at 25.9 %.  🔴 TIER-4 outlet, 2.0x the figure the publisher's own curve gives.  REFUSED, and filed as a gap: a successor quoting "Grand View" must say WHICH GVR series.

column1: # 🟢 THE RESULT, and it is a widening.

column2: $9.58 B - $12.3 B.  "A 28 % spread on the current year."

$3.05 B - $22.86 B.  SIX publishers, every one of them TIER-2 or TIER-3-carrying-TIER-2, every one of them arithmetically SELF-CONSISTENT under p274's classify() (5 PASS, 1 ROUNDING).  Spread: 7.5x, or 649 %.

🔴 The figures p377 sampled happened to cluster near $10 B.  The two that move the band are MarketsandMarkets at the bottom and Knowledge Sourcing at the top, and NEITHER can be refused: both are publisher-direct and both re-derive to their own labelled CAGR within 0.1 points.  🔵 So the disagreement is not a quality problem that grading can clean up.  It is DEFINITIONAL, exactly as p374 said, and the honest spread is 7.5x rather than the 28 % two passes have published.

column1: # 🔴 THE INSTRUMENT RESULT, which is the part a successor should take: the outlet instrument
# CANNOT pick a market number, and expecting it to was the error in p377-C's framing.

column2: Tier grading is a FILTER on attribution, not on definition.  It correctly refuses 5 figures that no publisher stands behind.  It cannot adjudicate between six publishers who each measure a different market competently.  🟢 Use it to refuse unsourced figures.  🔴 Never use it to narrow a definitional band.
